metaData.originalTitle: 当 Agent 替你值班：基于 Devix 构建 7x24 自动化运维 Harness Engineering
metaData.title: When the Agent Takes Your Shift: Building 7x24 Automated Operations with Devix - Harness Engineering
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article details a 7x24 automated operations system built on Devix, which uses Agent + script collaboration, a hierarchical decision engine, and a self-evolving rule mechanism to achieve an engineering closed loop for fault diagnosis, graded response, and continuous learning.
metaData.summary: The article from the Alibaba Cloud developer team documents how they used the Devix platform to build a complete automated operations system (Harness Engineering). Starting from the pain points of late-night alert dashboards, the author identifies three major problems with traditional manual operations: slowness, repetition, and discontinuity. It also argues against pure AI solutions, citing their instability and lack of memory. The core design philosophy is 'Agent handles semantic understanding and reasoning; scripts handle data retrieval and action execution,' forming a three-layer pipeline: semantic diagnosis layer (Agent), decision rule layer (script retrieval + Agent comprehensive decision), and action execution layer (scripts). The system runs as a 7x24 public service via Devix's cloud-resident Sandbox, integrating monitoring alerts, log parsing, correlation analysis, graded decision-making (auto-retry / button confirmation / code fix / investigation suggestion / escalate to human), DingTalk interaction, and case study accumulation. The article focuses on the confidence adjustment mechanism of the decision engine and the path of rule self-evolution (new rule discovery, effect evaluation, security audit), along with three security defenses. Finally, it summarizes key experiences: the Agent+script collaboration paradigm, trading confidence for automation level, and the self-evolving mechanism.

mainPoints.point: Agent + Script Collaboration Paradigm: Let the Agent handle semantic reasoning, let scripts handle deterministic operations.
mainPoints.explanation: The Agent is responsible for log parsing, root cause diagnosis, and rule matching, while all data retrieval and action execution (e.g., API calls, retries, GitLab archiving) are handled by deterministic scripts to ensure auditability and controllability.

mainPoints.point: Trading Confidence for Automation Level: Conservative handling for low experience, gradual expansion for high experience.
mainPoints.explanation: The system calculates the historical retry success rate from the case library, dynamically adjusts the diagnostic confidence, and then feeds it into the decision tree. New faults default to manual confirmation; after multiple successful handlings of the same type, the system automatically upgrades to fully automatic, achieving progressive trust.

mainPoints.point: Self-Evolving Rule Mechanism: The system continuously learns from its own experience.
mainPoints.explanation: Unmatched unknown cases are clustered by error code, then analyzed by the Agent to generate new rule drafts. Existing rules are monitored and revised based on retry success rates to prevent rule rigidity.

keyQuotes: The essence of Harness Engineering is not to make the Agent smarter, but to make it more controllable.

relatedArticles.title: Redefining Skill Development: A Step-by-Step Guide & One-Stop Development Assistant Launch

It also launches a one-stop Skill development assistant, skill-dev-aio, designed to free developers from tedious tool learning and allow them to focus on experience and judgment.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: OpenClaw and Hermes: A Comprehensive Review of AI Agent Architecture from Source Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically summarizes the design trade-offs and engineering practices of Agent architecture in core modules such as message routing, memory management, context engineering, and security sandboxing, through an in-depth analysis of the source code of two open-source AI Agent frameworks: OpenClaw and Hermes.

relatedArticles.title: A Practical Guide to 'Progressive Spec' for AI Coding in 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a 'Progressive Spec' framework for AI coding environments, leveraging structured documentation to drive AI collaboration and balance development standards with execution efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: From Toy to Productivity: Demystifying AI Agent Harness Engineering Through Real Projects
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the practical experience of the real-world project Aegis, this article systematically elaborates on the concept, architectural boundaries, and implementation methods of Harness Engineering. It argues that in enterprise engineering environments, constraining and governing non-deterministic large models by building a control plane is the key to transforming AI Agents from toys into productive tools, and it drives the migration of the engineer's role from code executor to goal controller.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.
